pages.text: Soso the quiet hedgehog chose fallen leaves on the slope, one by one. Red leaves and yellow leaves went onto the spines on their back. "When I have them all, I'll give them to Grandma."
Soso gathered the chosen leaves in one spot. The pile was as tall as Soso. An orange ribbon fluttered among the leaves. Just two more leaves to go.
Then Ppino ran over and jumped into the pile. Red and yellow leaves scattered everywhere. "Wow! Fun!" Kicking leaves, Ppino ran down the slope.
Soso forced a grin. "...It's okay." But their throat tightened, and their eyes burned. Soso curled up and hid inside their spines.
Curled Soso didn't move. Holding it in made their chest tighter. Only scattered leaves rustled below. The sun sank behind the peak.
Grandma Bear sat down heavily on the leaves beside Soso. Without a word, she patted her lap.
Soso uncurled and snuggled onto Grandma's lap. "Waaah!" The held-back tears burst out. Grandma patted their back. "Upset? It's okay to cry."
As the crying eased, the tight throat relaxed. Sniffling, Soso looked up from Grandma's lap. The orange ribbon fluttered again among the lowered spines.
Soso went to Ppino. "I was really upset earlier." "Sorry!" Ppino gathered the scattered leaves in both arms. After crying, the held-back words came out.
Soso offered Grandma the leaves they had gathered together again. Grandma hugged Soso. "Holding it in feels tight. Crying lets it feel clear." Soso smiled gently. "Upset? It's okay to cry!"
